_readme: THE RUN'S CONFIG — the pilot AND both sealed manifests. Dry run, then write:
--pilot-only emits the five pilot manifests alone and ignores manifestA/B, the run ids and
the pairs; it was the whole file until those were declared. A FULL build emits the pilot
manifests too, so read _beforeYouBuild item 2 before running one.
Keys beginning with _ are ignored by parseManifestConfig; they are notes for whoever fills
this in, and they are the ONLY place a pair's reason can live — the parser narrows every
abPairs entry to {id, taskId, order} and silently discards anything else.
EVERY PIN BELOW IS IN ONE OF THREE STATES, and the distinction is the point:
KNOWN HERE  - computed on the authoring machine and already filled in.
MAC-LOCAL   - null, because only the run machine can know it. The tool REFUSES on null;
a plausible-looking placeholder would VALIDATE, which is worse than a refusal.
CHOSEN      - the two constants thresholdArgument says have no ancestor. DECIDED 2026-08-12,
pre-data, with the reasoning and the refutation attempt in _chosenConstants.
Do not replace a null with a guess to make the tool quiet. The refusal is the deliverable.
Every remaining null is MAC-LOCAL. FOUR DECISIONS are open, plus one hazard that is not a
decision at all; all five are in _beforeYouBuild. An earlier version of this line said
nothing was open, which was true only while the sealed manifests did not exist.
_runIds: THREE NAMES, NOT PINS, and they are UNDATED ON PURPOSE. A run id is a path segment — it
names evidence/<runId>.b12.tasks.json — not a measurement, so the pin doctrine two blocks
down does not govern it. But an id carrying a date the run did not happen on is misleading
evidence in a file committed before the event, so these say `pending` instead. RENAME EACH
BEFORE `build`, the same instruction _pilotRunId already carries.
runIdA and runIdB MUST DIFFER (b12-manifest.mjs:348) — run 2 is a distinct registered run,
not a relabel. Manifest B's FILE is named from runIdA (outputPaths, b12-manifest.mjs:754);
runIdB is manifest B's own `runId`, the sole source open-b has for run 2's identity
(b12-register.mjs:856), AND — since 2026-08-13 — the id B's own pinned.scoringCommand is
resolved from, so runIdB now reaches past its own field. `plan` reads all three for parsing, manifest
construction and the output-path collision check, and writes none of them; `build` writes
them into manifest bytes and registration makes those bytes durable. So a rename is
mechanically free up to `build`. NOT impossible after it — `build` uses ordinary overwrite
for a path that has not yet entered history (b12-manifest.mjs:844). The irreversible boundary
is INTRODUCTION into history and registration, not the first build.
DECIDED 2026-08-13: rename all three IMMEDIATELY BEFORE `build`, with the real dates, and
leave `pending` until then. The alternative — dating them now — writes a claim about when the
run happened into a file committed before it happened, and the rename is free up to `build`
anyway. Since 2026-08-13 the ids also reach further than their own filenames: each manifest's
pinned.scoringCommand is resolved from its runId (_beforeYouBuild 3), so renaming after a
build and before registration means REBUILDING, not editing bytes.
_pilotRunId: Rename to the date the pilot actually runs. It names evidence/<pilotRunId>.b12.pilot-<taskId>.manifest.json and, after the run, evidence/<pilotRunId>.b12.pilot.json.
_pilot: ORDERED, and the order is load-bearing: committedOrderViolation runs for every treatment arm and is NOT under the pilotMode exemption, so each of these ships as its own single-task manifest with its task at index 0. All five are excluded from manifests A and B by design.artifacts 4.
_manifestsAandB: THE 30 + 30, COPIED FROM b12-corpus/corpus-plan.json AND NOT RETYPED. The order is
load-bearing: admissionRule 2 scores 'the first 20 that admit, in that committed order'.
NOTHING IN THE TOOLCHAIN COMPARES THESE LISTS TO THE PLAN — parseManifestConfig refuses
only A n B and A n pilot overlap. That is the duplication class that produced a real defect
four commits ago, when nothing compared the 60 written specs to the plan they came from
(b637461). tests/b12-plan.test.ts now binds this file to corpus-plan.json for exactly that
reason, along with specRoot and the ratesSha256 that is also stated in both places.
_abPairs: SIX PAIRS PER MANIFEST. A pair is ONE TASK RUN TWICE — once with the delegation server
installed, once without — and `order` says which arm goes first.
SIX IN A IS FROZEN (b12-register.mjs:95, runPlan PHASE 7 '12 sessions (6 pairs)'). SIX IN B
IS CHOSEN. B's count is not unchecked — manifestDeclarationGaps enforces a minimum of three
at assembly and before every observation (b12-run.mjs:1106, :2565) — but nothing requires
exactly six of it, and open-b does not re-run checkCore. Six keeps the scored run under the
cardinality PHASE 7 froze whichever manifest ends up scored, AT A COST: if B opens, that is
six more paid sessions than the minimum-valid three would have been.
THE SELECTION IS: THE FIRST SIX IDS OF THE COMMITTED ORDER. That is the whole rule. It has
no clauses to tune, and its shape is not mine — admissionRule 2 already scores 'the first 20
that admit, in that committed order', so a prefix is the selection this design uses on the
primary instrument. The pairs use the same shape on the same order.
THE 3/3 STRATUM SPLIT IS A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A TERM: the plan interleaves strata (b12-plan.mjs
deals alternately within each), so the first six are three test-red and three types-only
without the rule mentioning strata at all.
TWO EARLIER SELECTIONS WERE DISCARDED, and both failures are worth keeping because the second
is subtler than the first.
A HAND-PICKED LIST, rejected because its stated reason was that chkbudget and chkdetect run
the loudest suite and a loud control arm pushes R_ab AWAY from the kill. That is selection
on expected outcome — the residual task-selection channel operatorConfound says it cannot
close — and a falsification-only instrument does not neutralise it, because avoiding the
kill is itself valuable to the operator.
A RULE WITH A fileScope CLAUSE ('take a task if its stratum has fewer than three slots AND
its fileScope is not already used'), rejected for a better reason: adversarial review
pointed out that removing outcome vocabulary from a rule does not remove the degree of
freedom that SELECTED the rule, and named a rule of equal simplicity — first, middle and
last per stratum — that would have included chkdetect. The fileScope clause was the tunable
part, and it was the clause doing the work.
THE HONEST RESIDUAL, since a rule adopted after its output is known is weaker than a
pre-committed one: the outcome space HAS been seen, and no rule chosen now can undo that.
What a prefix buys is that it is the rule with the fewest places to hide — there is one way
to write 'the first six', and the alternative rules that were considered and their outputs
are recorded above rather than deleted.
WHAT THE PREFIX COSTS, taken as it came rather than patched:
- MANIFEST A GETS NO ESCAPE-ROUTE PAIR. Its first six hold none of the seven types-only
sites that admit a tsc-green fix which changes behaviour; manifest B's first six hold two
(tylmsopt, typarseblk). An earlier draft added a clause to fix exactly this, and that
clause is what review rejected. So the escape route is observable in B and not in A.
- CONCENTRATED SCOPES. A's six touch only three files, three of them src/selection.ts; B's
touch four. Two of A's pairs share tests/selection.test.ts, so one flaky suite can take
two of its six, and voidConditions 21 voids the whole A/B below three complete pairs.
- ALL THREE types-only pairs in each manifest share `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` by
construction, so a tsc that cannot run takes three at once.
ARM ORDER alternates WITHIN stratum — test-red opening treatment-first, types-only opening
control-first — giving 3/3 per manifest. Alternating by POSITION instead would have been
simpler and is wrong: the committed order alternates strata, so every test-red pair would
have been treatment-first and every types-only pair control-first, perfectly confounding arm
order with stratum. Which stratum opens with which arm is arbitrary and is not defended.
WHAT 3/3 DOES AND DOES NOT BOUND: it balances WITHIN-PAIR position, first arm against second.
It does not bound chronological drift across pairs, because the manifest declares each pair's
arm order but NOT the sequence in which pairs are run — b12-run.mjs:1130 leaves that to the
A/B pass, and committedOrderViolation covers treatment arms only.
ON THE ESCAPE ROUTE, corrected from a claim that was too strong. Pairing makes the same defect
and the same predicate available in BOTH arms, but availability is not probability. Only the
treatment arm has `repair`, which loops until its checks pass, and on a tsc-only task that
loop has no signal separating a restored annotation from a behaviour-changing patch
(src/tools/repair.ts:628, :722). Arm-dependent route choice therefore survives as a possible
TREATMENT EFFECT or confound. Pairing does not close the question; it makes the route
observable in both arms for two of the seven, both of them in B.
MEASURED about what the validators do NOT require, so nothing above reads as enforced: pair
taskIds need not be distinct (six pairs may name one task), pair ids are held to no grammar
and reach no path, and NOTHING ties a pair to the admission window. Every property here is
chosen, and tests/b12-plan.test.ts derives this rule's exact output so a drift from it is red.
_beforeYouBuild: TWO THINGS ARE NOT SETTLED, and neither is which tasks to pair. `plan` is silent on both, so
a clean dry run is not evidence that `build` and then `register` can succeed. Two others WERE
settled on 2026-08-13 and are recorded here as decisions, with what they cost.
1. THE HARNESS SEAL DOES NOT EXIST. evidence/b12-harness-seal.json is a barrier before ANY
registration (b12-register.mjs:642 and :749). It comes from a fourth verb —
`node scripts/b12-register.mjs seal-harness <runId> [manifestPath]` (:800) — which
defaults manifestPath to evidence/<runId>.b12.tasks.json and so must run AFTER `build`.
It refuses an on-disk file and an addition reachable through the CURRENT revision's
history, then creates with exclusive `wx` (:545, :580). Not `--all`: unreachable history
would not stop it. The order is: fill the MAC-LOCAL pins -> build -> seal-harness ->
commit -> register. DECIDED: run it last, once everything else here is settled — it is
create-only forever.
2. THE FIVE PILOT MANIFESTS MUST NOT BE COMMITTED, and item 4 turned that from convenient
into forced. A full `build` re-emits them (b12-manifest.mjs:814) and refuses on any output
path already TRACKED at HEAD (:823) — a guard above the `if (write)` branch, so it applies
to `plan` too. evidence/ is not gitignored, so committing them is the natural act and
would make the later build refuse on all five.
THE ESCAPE THIS FILE USED TO NAME — "a different pilotRunId" — IS NOT ONE ANY MORE. Now
that manifestObject emits pilotRunId into A and B, a fresh id makes manifest A name a
pilot record that does not exist: the pilot wrote evidence/<old id>.b12.pilot.json
(b12-run.mjs:2315) and the register reads the path manifest A names (:740). The real
escape is a new pilot RUN — pick an unborn pilotRunId, re-emit its manifests, RE-RUN all
five pilot sessions, commit the resulting pilot record, then build A/B with that same id.
It costs five sessions. The cheap version is an identity that lies.
SEQUENCE: --pilot-only -> run the pilot -> leave the five manifests UNTRACKED -> full
build with the SAME pilotRunId. Note `build` uses ordinary overwrite for a path not yet in
history (:844), so it silently replaces an untracked pilot manifest, which is what makes
the sequence work.
3. DECIDED — pinned.scoringCommand IS A TEMPLATE, resolved per manifest by the assembler
(b12-manifest.mjs, pinnedFor) from that manifest's OWN runId. It used to name the PILOT
run, and one literal string cannot be right for A, for B and for both of emit's
invocations: clause 19 compares exact equality against an invocation rebuilt from the
WHOLE argv (assemble.ts:1172, emit.ts:316), and the prescribed loop emits twice per run
(audit.ts:15). Build-time checking is presence-only (b12-run.mjs:1065), so a wrong value
used to seal in silence; the assembler now refuses a template carrying no <runId>.
THE TEMPLATE PINS THE FINAL FORM, WITH --audit, AND THAT HAS A PRICE. One of the two
invocations must diverge from the pin. Pinning the bare form would void the FINAL scored
artifact, which is fatal; pinning the --audit form voids the FIRST instead — already
final:false with clauses 4-6 UNCHECKED, and overwritten by step 7. So step 2 of the loop
commits a result.json carrying verdict:"void", and that is expected, not a fault.
HAZARD A: that provisional void makes the run look CONCLUDED to the REGISTRATION gate.
collectRegister reads the committed result (archive.ts:646) and narrowPriorRun turns a
void into a NON-NULL prior result (:689), while the gate blocks only prior runs whose
result is null (b12-register.mjs:607). Between steps 2 and 7 a second run can therefore be
registered against a run with no final audited result, and an operator who never reaches
step 7 has spent an attempt on a provisional void. It cannot OPEN B — open-b demands
verdict === "open" (b12-register.mjs:837) and a void is not that.
HAZARD B IS THE ONE THAT OPENS B, and it is worse for exactly that reason: narrowPriorRun
and open-b both ignore result.final. Running the pinned --audit command BEFORE the audit is
committed does NOT fire clause 19 — the string matches — the audit is refused, gitAudit.ran
goes false, and the verdict can be a perfectly ordinary `open` that is NOT FINAL. open-b
accepts it. RULE, covering both: no registration and no `open-b` until the final
result.json with final:true is committed.
The terminal does say NOT FINAL (emit.ts:352). The committed JSON is what every later
check reads, and it does not ask.
RUN emit FROM THE REPOSITORY ROOT. invocationString is path.relative(cwd, argv[1])
(emit.ts:317), so any other cwd spells a different string and voids on clause 19.
AND THE PRE-REGISTRATION DISAGREES WITH THE HARNESS ABOUT THE COUNT. runPlan PHASE 6 says
"One scoring invocation over the ARCHIVE, never the live directory, using the committed
command string"; audit.ts:15-21 prescribes two emits, each of which reassembles and writes
both artifacts. Both texts are in this repository and they cannot both be obeyed. Which
one governs is the owner's call and is NOT decided here.
4. DECIDED — manifestObject emits pilotRunId into A and B. b12-register.mjs:627 and :740
resolve the pilot as `manifestA?.pilotRunId ?? runId` and the field was never emitted, so
the fallback always fired and the register looked for the pilot under the RUN's id. Two
repairs existed: bend runIdA to equal pilotRunId, or emit the field. The second was taken
— bending the id propagates one accident into three places nothing compares. NOT emitted
on the five pilot manifests, where nothing reads it and it would only restate runId.
ALSO OPEN — a HAZARD rather than a decision, and worse for manifest B than its pair count:
B carries the same DECLARED claudeCodeVersion and claudeBinarySha256 as A — the same
declaration, no longer literally A's object, since scoringCommand is now resolved onto a copy
per manifest (b12-manifest.mjs, pinnedFor) — and
assertPinned refuses at EVERY observe on a mismatch (b12-run.mjs:888). If Claude Code updates
between run 1 and run 2 — weeks apart by design — run 2 can only proceed on the PINNED binary, which may mean restoring it. B cannot be re-sealed for a new one.

_knownHere.ratesSha256: sha256 of .local-coder/rates.json at the shared green parent. Compared inside EACH base commit's own tree by assertRatesFrozen, so it is a property of the corpus, not of a machine.
_knownHere.b12RunSha256: sha256 of scripts/b12-run.mjs at 608e930. GOES STALE THE MOMENT THAT FILE CHANGES — observe asserts the running harness IS the sealed one, so recompute if you touch it before the run.
_knownHere.claudeMdSha256: sha256 of the in-repo CLAUDE.md at 608e930.
_knownHere.scoringCommand: A TEMPLATE, not the pinned string. <runId> is substituted per manifest by the assembler (b12-manifest.mjs, pinnedFor) so each of the seven carries ONE literal command, which is what voidConditions 19 compares. B resolves to runIdB, not to the runIdA its sealed FILE is named from. Change the template here and nowhere else; the assembler refuses a template with no <runId>.
_knownHere.perArmTimeoutMs: 45 minutes. Declared rather than left to the silent fallback, which manifestDeclarationGaps refuses.
_knownHere.extraArgs: Empty, deliberately: a non-empty value forces an installedChars RE-PROBE (b12-run.mjs:1911).

_macLocal.claudeCodeVersion: The FULL x.y.z on the run machine. assertPinned compares with .includes(), so a partial pin like 2.1.2 silently matches 2.1.221 — the assembler refuses anything that is not x.y.z.  claude --version
_macLocal.claudeBinarySha256: sha256 of the Claude Code binary that will run.  shasum -a 256 $(which claude)
_macLocal.clientTruncationCap: The cap MEASURED for that version. voidConditions 8 VOIDS a run with no cap measured for the version that ran.  scripts/b12-truncationcap-probe-mac.sh
_macLocal.settingsSha256s: BOTH keys required, and null is a legitimate value meaning 'this file does not exist' — omission declares nothing, null declares an absence. NOT MAC-LOCAL, which is why `settings` is filled: instructionHashesAt hashes .claude/settings.json out of each ARM's detached worktree (b12-run.mjs:2815), and those worktrees come from the corpus tags, so this is a property of the published trees and is knowable here. MEASURED across all 65 b12/corpus/* tags: every one carries .claude/settings.json as blob 34994e4f, 432 bytes, sha256 75cd35da…4d867d; none carries .claude/settings.local.json, so settingsLocal stays null and that null is TRUE. It was null before, which declared an absence that is false. Mechanically it would have sealed either way — b12-run.mjs:1068 shape-checks the keys and nothing ever compares these values to instructionHashesAt — so this is a correction to what the file SAYS, not a refusal that was being dodged.
_macLocal.installedCharsProbe: Path to the committed probe artifact, plus its sha256. The re-probe is OWED with the orchestrator model in the calibration key (PREMISES.md, sixth decision).  scripts/b12-installedchars-probe-mac.sh
_macLocal.mcpConfig: Path to the generated MCP config, plus its sha256. observe dereferences both and NO validator checks them; the path is machine-local, so presence is all this machine can assert.
_macLocal.policyBlobs: One {repo, commit, path, sha256} per arm, for the OUT-OF-REPO policy bundles. The repo must exist on the run machine, be a full (not shallow) clone, and resolve OUTSIDE this repository — findPolicyBlob refuses an in-repo path as in-repo policy wearing an out-of-repo name.
_macLocal.memorySnapshot: Directory of the memory snapshot, plus its sha256. FOUND LATE AND WORTH SAYING WHY: observe REQUIRES this (b12-run.mjs:1690, citing voidConditions 13) and manifestDeclarationGaps never asks for it — so before the assembler was taught to check it, a manifest could pass every build-time check in this repository and then refuse on the run machine.
_macLocal.captureSha256: sha256 of the built dist/ capture. Its absence is SILENTLY PERMISSIVE rather than refusing: observe compares only `if (want)` (b12-run.mjs:2040), so leaving it null-and-unfilled means the capture ships unverified. STATE.md's standing note — re-pin this at the seal — is the same instruction from the other end.

_chosenConstants._status: DECIDED 2026-08-12, pre-data, before any B12 observation exists. thresholdArgument calls these the two numbers 'this design must set that have no ancestor' and requires them 'declared as chosen rather than derived'. Both values below were adversarially reviewed against nine enumerated claims and SEVEN of the nine were sustained against the author; the ceiling moved from 0.85 to 0.95 as a result. What survives is recorded here, corrections included, because a justification that hides its refuted version is worth less than the number it defends.

pacingCacheWriteShareCeiling.what_it_does: admissionRule 11's second half. pacingFacts (src/cost/b12/assemble.ts:150-158) prices ONLY the observation's originatedRequestIds (:588-589) and fires on a STRICT >. voidConditions 20 then lifts it from an observation-level disposition to a run-level one: buildArchiveChecks pushes the clause when ANY assessed observation exceeded (:1187-1198), and assemble.ts:454-455 sets verdict='void' when ANY archive check fired. So one observation over this ceiling VOIDS ALL ~60 SESSIONS, and the experiment has two attempts total. Note `assessed`, not `admitted`: an observation already dropped for task_failed still counts here, and the only escape is an unreadable observation.json or an unrebuildable transcript (:567-586).
pacingCacheWriteShareCeiling.the_finding_that_set_it: THE STATISTIC CANNOT SEPARATE THE TWO CASES IT IS ASKED TO SEPARATE. A legitimately SHORT observation is structurally near the top of the range: its first request writes the whole context and nothing has re-read it yet. Measured over per-session groups on this machine: 1 request -> 0.8841, 2 requests -> 0.7732, 3 -> 0.7610. An all-rewrite PATHOLOGY at a long session lands at 0.93-0.98. The bands OVERLAP, so no value is safe in both directions. Given that, the ceiling is set above the legitimate-short envelope, because the erring-low error costs a paid attempt immediately while the erring-high error is covered by the gap half -- which catches the phone-call scenario admissionRule 11 actually names, directly and independently.
pacingCacheWriteShareCeiling.why_not_0_85: That was this file's first answer and it is wrong. It was chosen against a population filtered to >=2 requests, which excluded the very shape that binds. Nothing guarantees a B12 observation makes ten requests, or two: validity requires only a nonzero originated count (scripts/b12-run.mjs:2988-3012). A single-request observation measured 0.8841 here, so 0.85 would have voided the run on a legitimate one.
pacingCacheWriteShareCeiling.why_not_higher_still: It must remain a check. With cacheWrite at the 1h class's 2.0x and output at 5.0x, an all-rewrite session has share 2N/(2N+5o+i); solving strictly with o=1500, i=200 gives N > 21,816.7 at c=0.85, N > 34,650 at 0.90 and N > 73,150 at 0.95. At the 5m class's 1.25x the same three are 34,907 / 55,440 / 117,040. So 0.95 still fires on a 45-minute coding observation rewriting a 73k context at 1h rates; it is weak at 5m rates, and that is exactly the case where the gap bar drops to five minutes and the gap half becomes twelve times more sensitive. The two halves cover each other in opposite regimes.
pacingCacheWriteShareCeiling.the_error_this_takes: NOT that erring high is free -- an earlier draft claimed that and it is false. Undetected inflation lowers R, and a lower R makes a FALL easier, which the design's bracket reading (R_hi+ for the fall) exists to prevent. Separately, inflation in the CONTROL arm raises R_ab = sum(A_control - A_treatment)/sum(A_control) -- and no value of this constant covers that, because primary assembly filters to arm === 'treatment' (assemble.ts:221-222) and control observations are never pacing-assessed at all. The error is taken knowingly, in exchange for not spending a paid attempt on a false positive.

perTaskDenominatorShareCap.what_it_does: NOTHING MECHANICAL, and that is checked, not assumed: perTaskDenominatorShare is computed at assemble.ts:845 and typed at types.ts:1028, and NO code anywhere reads perTaskDenominatorShareCap -- the only mention outside this file is the comment at assemble.ts:843 saying it decides nothing, 'a live predicate here would mint a void the frozen text never wrote'. manifestDeclarationGaps still REQUIRES it (b12-run.mjs:1061-1064), so it is a pre-commitment published on the manifest's face and compared by a reader, not by the scorer.
perTaskDenominatorShareCap.why_0_25: Because it costs nothing when it fires, it is chosen tight and meaningful rather than safe. The denominator is admittedSumAPlusSLo over the ADMITTED set, which assemble.ts:389-405 caps at 20 treatment observations, one per task id -- so the EQUAL share is 1/20 = 0.05 and 0.25 is five times it. STATED WITH ITS CONDITION, because the review sustained the correction: shares are weighted by each task's A+S_lo, not by observation counts, so '0.25 equals a minimum evaluable stratum of MIN_DELIVERY_OBSERVATIONS = 5' holds only if those five weigh the same as the others. What is unconditionally true is the multiple: 0.25 is 5x the equal share, and a task at it carries the weight five average ones would.
perTaskDenominatorShareCap.expected_to_fire: Yes, sometimes, and that is the intent. If one task costs 10x the median while the rest sit at it, its share is 10/29 = 0.34 and the reader is told so. A covariate that never fires reports nothing.

_refutation.predicted_before_measuring: Written to a file before any measurement ran. Median cacheWrite share 0.15-0.45 (HELD, 0.3042); p95 below 0.80 (HELD, 0.6916); a healthy session above 0.85 (recorded FAILED, then TRUE after all -- the first pass filtered to >=2 requests and hid the single-request case at 0.8841); max above 0.90 (FAILED, 0.8841 is the highest measured). The pre-registered falsification rule said that if nothing healthy sat above 0.85 then 0.95 was unearned slack and had to be dropped. It was dropped -- and then restored, when the excluded subpopulation turned out to be the one that binds. The prediction's ARITHMETIC about short sessions was right; its POPULATION was wrong, and the second error hid the first.
_refutation.method: cacheWrite units / total billed units over 160 Claude Code transcripts, replicating readUsage's 'equal or nothing' TTL split (src/cost/transcript.ts:201-241), rates.json's multipliers, api-error exclusion, one row per requestId. Run twice: per FILE, then per sessionId -- the second because pacingFacts prices only originatedRequestIds, and a whole-file group can carry inherited requests it would exclude. Grouping tighter did not move the tail (max 0.7732 either way for >=2 requests), which is the answer to that attack rather than an assumption about it.
_refutation.what_this_is_not: Not derived from any B12 observation -- none exists. But NOT 'unfitted' either, and the review was right to press: the historical data set the lower edge of the window this value sits in, and the arithmetic set the upper edge. The value is chosen inside that window. That is the honest label, and it is narrower than the first draft's claim.

_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk._why_this_block_exists: The OTHER half of admissionRule 11 -- max inter-request gap > the shortest cache TTL in play -- has NO constant to choose and is a larger threat to a paid run than either number above. It is recorded here because deciding the two constants is not the same as covering pacing, and reading this file could otherwise leave the opposite impression.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.the_bar_is_5_MINUTES_whenever_anyFiveMin: pacingFacts sets anyFiveMin when ANY owned request has cacheWrite5m > 0, and TTL_MS then selects 300,000 ms over 3,600,000 (assemble.ts:147-148). TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES SET IT, and neither is under this file's control:
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.route_1_a_subagent: ALREADY MEASURED ON THE MAC, today: MEASUREMENTS.jsonl:239 (run 2026-08-12-mac-b12-subagentkey-77fddca) records 9,397 subagent cache_creation tokens in the 5m class against 0 on the main thread, whose writes were 1h. So an observation carrying a subagent gets a five-minute pacing bar. That row also records that this FALSIFIED the earlier reading from the installedChars probe, which saw 7 records with no ephemeral_5m and concluded pacing was probably defused -- those 7 had no subagent. n = 1 subagent, one session: not established that every subagent writes 5m.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.route_2_an_inconsistent_split: MEASURED HERE and not previously named anywhere: readUsage returns cacheWrite5m = total when the TTL split disagrees with its own top-level cache_creation_input_tokens (transcript.ts:232-238), so an INCONSISTENT record books its whole write to the 5m class and sets anyFiveMin -- with no real 5m write involved. 144 of 81,979 assistant records in this machine's corpus (0.18%) have such a split. One of them inside an observation's owned set is enough to drop that observation's bar to five minutes.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.what_that_costs: On the 1h bar, only 0.44% of 33,894 historical inter-request gaps exceed it and the 15 largest are 18h-186h RESUMES, which a harness-spawned session cannot have -- observe mints a fresh --session-id per observation and never resumes. On the 5m bar, 4.01% of the same gaps exceed it. voidConditions 20 makes ONE exceeding observation void the whole run.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.what_is_NOT_established: That a harness-driven, non-interactive observation idles the way a human-driven session does. The historical gaps include a human thinking and typing; a B12 observation has no human in the loop and its gaps are tool-execution times. This is the single largest unquantified risk to the paid run, and it is not resolvable from Windows -- but it is also not resolvable by choosing either constant above, which is the point of recording it here rather than pretending a ceiling covers it.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.IF_THE_GAPS_ARE_TOOL_TIMES_THEN_OUR_OWN_: ADDED 2026-08-14, following the line above to its conclusion. The block already says a B12 observation's gaps ARE tool-execution times. This repository ships the tools, so their durations are the gap distribution, and two of them are measured. THE COINCIDENCE IS EXACT: repair's DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS is 300 (src/tools/repair.ts:133) and TTL_MS['5m'] is 300_000 (assemble.ts:116) -- the default budget of a treatment-only tool IS the five-minute bar, and pacingFacts compares with a strict >. A repair call that spends its budget therefore lands on the bar and any overhead puts it over.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.and_the_gate_alone_already_exceeds_it_on: MEASURED 2026-08-13, six full gate runs on the authoring machine: npm-test took 348, 377, 547, 554, 576 and 673 seconds, and a seventh through scripts/b12-gate-pace.mjs took 650. Every one of those is a single inter-request gap of 5.8 to 11.2 minutes. On the ubuntu-latest CI runner the identical suite is 20.3 s wall, so this is Windows process-spawn cost and NOT a property of the suite.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.AND_THE_RUN_MACHINE_HAS_NOW_ANSWERED_gat: MEASURED 2026-08-14 on mac-01 with the same instrument, six calls across two trees. At HEAD (78a7585): 53.8, 55.3, 58.0 s -- MAX 19% of the 300,000 ms bar. At the corpus base b12/corpus/selmatchfuzzy (98becdf), which is the tree an observation actually sees: 32.1, 32.3, 33.6 s -- MAX 11%. Nothing came within 5x of the bar. PREDICTED 30-90 s under the bar at ~70% confidence before the run; measured 58.0. A single gate call therefore CANNOT by itself produce an over-bar gap on the machine that will run the sessions, and the win-01 numbers above are a Windows property rather than a threat to the paid run.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.what_is_still_open_is_repair_and_it_is_n: The gate being fast does not touch repair, because repair's 300,000 ms is a BUDGET and not a duration: it loops the gate until the checks pass or the deadline expires (repair.ts:629-646, DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS = 300, repairMaxRounds 3 at b12-spec.mjs:107). repair is treatment-only, so the exposure is ARM-DEPENDENT.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.AND_THAT_MEASUREMENT_IS_IN_2026_08_14_th: mac-01, three runRepair calls on b12/corpus/selmatchfuzzy with the 30B pinned and the task's own fileScope and prompt: 129.4, 115.6, 120.1 s, every one FIXED in ONE round. Per round, median: model 57.6 s + gate 31.8 s = 89.4 s. THE ONE-ROUND TOTAL IS NOT THE MARGIN. The bar exists for the case repairMaxRounds allows, and three rounds is 268 s at the median round and 293 s at the worst observed one (65.8 + 31.9) -- 89 to 98 PERCENT of the 300,000 ms bar. So the route is not closed; it is quantified, and the margin is 2 to 11 percent rather than the 57 the one-round runs suggest. Worse in the way this block already predicted before it had numbers: repair spends three rounds precisely on the HARD tasks, which are the same ones that produce void(task_failed), so the two void routes correlate.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.DECIDED_2026_08_14_budget_seconds_240: TAKEN, pre-data, before any observation exists. DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS in src/tools/repair.ts goes 300 -> 240. At 300 the default WAS the five-minute bar exactly, so a repair that spent its budget put an observation's largest gap at the edge of it; 240 leaves 2.7 rounds at the measured rate and puts a full-budget repair 20 percent clear. THE COST IS REAL AND ONE-SIDED: repair is treatment-only, so this trims the arm being measured and not its control -- a deliberate bias AGAINST the treatment, which is the safe direction for a cost claim in the treatment's favour. Enforced at the DEFAULT rather than declared in a manifest, because a session that omits the argument gets it and cannot forget. NOT the specs: they carry repairMaxRounds and no budget, and the 65 bases are published.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.what_it_costs_elsewhere: src/tools/repair.ts is not in clause 5's PINNED_PATHS (src/cost/, src/telemetry.ts, scripts/b12-run.mjs), so the edit is lawful pre-data -- and the adversarial review below confirmed the only transitive cover is the b12:emission FENCE (audit.ts:63-108 over repair.ts:493-509 and :986-1091), which ced2261's two hunks (130-164, 755-795) do not touch. It DOES change the built dist/, so pinned.captureSha256 must be recomputed at the seal -- which STATE.md already lists. It also breaks a tie the code relied on: config.timeoutMs stays at 300 s, so the budget is now strictly smaller and min(timeoutMs, remaining) resolves to the budget. THIS KEY ORIGINALLY SAID both stale statements were corrected where they lived, in repair.ts and tests/repair.test.ts. THAT WAS FALSE and the review caught it: four more sites still asserted the old default or the tie -- the MCP input schema's own description (repair.ts:59, the one a session actually reads), the model_failed comment (repair.ts:876-882), the dead-heat test's rationale (tests/repair.test.ts:1073-1074), and PREMISES.md:1527. All four corrected 2026-08-14 in the follow-up commit.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.still_NOT_established: That other tasks generate at this rate. selmatchfuzzy edits one file and its fix is one character, and the measurement is one task on an unloaded machine. WHAT IS NOW SETTLED, and was not when this key was written: no corpus task has a larger fileScope. MEASURED 2026-08-14 over all 65 spec.json files -- the fileScope histogram is {1: 65}, every task exactly one file. So the 'larger fileScope means less margin' worry does not apply to any admitted observation; it applies to PHASE 3's own units, where it is real and recorded in PREMISES.md.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.a_second_thing_the_same_six_runs_settled: The suite is DETERMINISTIC on the run machine: 3 of 3 green at HEAD, and 3 of 3 red at the corpus base with the SAME 7 failures every time -- which is the injected defect behaving, not the 0-to-9 nondeterminism win-01 shows across six full runs of identical bytes. Clause 6's suite attestation runs on the Mac, so the flake recorded in MEASUREMENTS.jsonl is an authoring-machine problem and not a risk to the attestation.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.why_this_is_worse_than_a_symmetric_risk: repair is a TREATMENT-ONLY tool and it loops the gate under a deadline (repair.ts:629-646), so the arm that carries the delegation is the arm with the long tool calls. The exposure is therefore ARM-DEPENDENT, which is the shape of a confound and not merely of a hazard. Worse, repair spends its full budget exactly when the task is hard -- the same tasks that produce void(task_failed) -- so the two void routes CORRELATE, and a hard task can take the whole run down instead of just its own observation. NOT RESOLVABLE BY PROTOCOL: lowering budget_seconds under the bar weakens repair and biases against the treatment; leaving it weakens nothing and risks the run. Both are pre-data design decisions, and neither is an operator instruction.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_2026_08_14_of_ced2261: Five enumerated claims put to Codex against the named commit; four came back CONFIRMED and one REFUTED. ADJUDICATED, not accepted on sight, and every file:line re-checked by hand. UPHELD: (3) stale tie assertions and (4) the schema description still advertising 'default 300' -- both real, both fixed, and (4) is the one that mattered most because the MCP input schema is what a treatment session reads to decide how long it may spend. REFUTED and the refutation upheld: (2) clause 5 -- the fence check above is the evidence. Claims (1) and (5) are dealt with in their own keys below. WHAT THE REVIEW DID NOT FIND, and was found by following its citation: PREMISES.md:1527 also asserted the old default. Corrected there. WHAT I THEN GOT WRONG IN THAT SAME CORRECTION, and fixed the same day: I wrote that the PHASE 3 entry's recorded truncation of the registered max_rounds gets TIGHTER at 240, and that the next exposure 'must pass budget_seconds explicitly and is still not done'. Neither holds. b12-scorer-mac.sh pins budget_seconds: 600 and max_rounds: 3 in the prompt (:255, :933-934), pins LOCAL_CODER_TIMEOUT_MS: 180000 into the MCP config and refuses to run if it does not land (:660-662), and VOIDs any unit whose telemetry row shows other limits or none (:1102-1110). An explicit argument beats the default, so the 300 -> 240 move cannot reach a PHASE 3 exposure at all. The error was asserting a gap without reading the harness that closes it; both sites now say so rather than being quietly rewritten.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.CLAIM_1_the_budget_is_not_a_bound_on_the: CONFIRMED, and the comment that said otherwise was mine. repair.ts:659 read 'a hard deadline for the whole call'; it is a deadline for the LOOP. `started` is taken at repair.ts:391 but the deadline is only built at :663, so the preflight between them is unchecked (it does consume the budget, so a slow one starves the loop rather than extending it); and after the loop, restore (:961), the second treeFingerprint (:964) and the telemetry write (:992) all run uncapped. Both tails scale with files.length, which the schema does not cap. WHY IT DOES NOT THREATEN THE 300 s BAR HERE: Codex's concrete scenario is 1,000 files, and the corpus fileScope histogram is {1: 65} -- one file, every task. At one file both tails are a git spawn apiece, about 200 ms measured, so a full-budget call lands at ~240 s. NOT CLOSED, LABELLED: a session passes `files` itself and is not bound to the spec's fileScope, so the bound is 240 s plus work the caller sizes. Cheap to close (thread remainingMs through rollback and fingerprint); not done, because no measured caller is near the bar.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.CLAIM_5_the_one_sidedness_claim_was_too_: PARTLY UPHELD. The claim being attacked was mine: that a treatment-only tool getting a smaller budget can only bias AGAINST the treatment, which is the safe direction. UPHELD AGAINST ME -- there is a channel the other way, through selection and not through cost. Admission requires disposition === 'scored' (assemble.ts:379-407) and a repair that fails can end the task at void(task_failed) (assemble.ts:680-686); the loop then walks the committed order and the next task takes the slot, so tasks the treatment arm cannot finish leave the admitted set instead of scoring badly in it. A weaker repair raises that attrition rate. THE MECHANISM IS REAL; THE SIGN IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Codex asserts the dropped tasks are 'difficult, low-saving' and offers nothing for the correlation between difficulty and saving -- and that correlation is the whole sign. It is not measured, and no observation exists to measure it from. Note also that the channel predates the change: it is the same at 300, and 240 only moves a rate. DECLINED, with reason: Codex's second mechanism, that a shorter call avoids the pacing void and so 'preferentially preserves a run capable of reporting a treatment-favouring result'. voidConditions 20 is RUN-level and kills both arms together, so avoiding it does not select on R's value -- it selects on whether any number exists at all, which is the stated purpose of the change and not a bias in it.
_theGapHalfIsTheBiggerRisk.THE_PIN_THAT_CAUGHT_IT_2026_08_14: SECOND CONSEQUENCE OF EDITING A PINNED PATH, AND I DID NOT ANTICIPATE IT. Commits 8fedebc and 4f0e0de changed scripts/b12-run.mjs, and pinned.b12RunSha256 went stale: b12-plan.test.ts:131 compares it against shaAt("HEAD", "scripts/b12-run.mjs") and went red with a real AssertionError, not the over-budget flake. The test's own comment says "Going red here is the alarm working", and it was. Re-pinned here 053eb27932e4 -> e91c268a0f29. LAWFUL ONLY BECAUSE IT IS PRE-DATA: the config's note says the harness seal freezes b12RunSha256 permanently, so after the seal this is not a re-pin but a clause-5 event. AND A LESSON ABOUT THE VERIFICATION LOOP, not about the code: the assertion reads HEAD, so a full suite run BEFORE the commit lands cannot see it — both offending commits were gated green pre-commit and were red the moment they existed. Any future edit to a pinned path must re-pin IN THE SAME COMMIT, which is what this one does.

_whichModelRunsIsDecidedByRAM._why_this_block_exists: The treatment arm's power depends on WHICH local model runs, and nothing here pins one. `selection` takes 'the largest catalog model fitting usable free RAM', so the answer is decided at run time by whatever else is open on the machine. Across ~60 sessions over one to two weeks the model can change underneath the run and no pin would notice: `pinned` carries no model field. An arm whose model depends on free RAM is not one arm.
_whichModelRunsIsDecidedByRAM.measured_on_mac_01_2026_08_14: runStatus over the built-in catalog: mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-dwq-v2 -> qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct-dwq-v2, available true, match fuzzy, FITS FALSE; qwen2.5-coder-14b-instruct -> qwen2.5-coder-14b-instruct-mlx@8bit, available true, fits true. auto_selection took the 14B, reason 'largest catalog model fitting usable free RAM (14.6 GB)'. The occupied RAM was the PREVIOUS round's model still resident in LM Studio -- `lms unload --all` is now the first thing scripts/b12-repair-pace.mjs does. Both entries resolving also REFUTES an alarm raised the same day that a catalogue/served id mismatch might degrade the treatment arm silently.
_whichModelRunsIsDecidedByRAM.the_csv_route_is_CLOSED_and_1eba3dc_is_w: Pointing LOCAL_CODER_MODELS_CSV at a one-row catalogue looks like the obvious pin and was proposed here on 2026-08-14. It is the route commit 1eba3dc closed. That variable was set in ~/.claude.json for run mac-07 against a file that DID NOT EXIST; loadModelCatalog fell back to the built-in catalogue with a warning nobody read, and a MEASUREMENTS row recorded the requested catalogue instead of the one in force -- 'the variable being set says what was requested, not what took effect'. The fix was to let the built-in catalogue in models-csv.ts be the one in force, because a catalogue inside the repository is reproducible from a commit and a path on somebody's disk is neither pinnable nor hashable. Re-proposing the CSV would undo that and reinstate its failure mode.
_whichModelRunsIsDecidedByRAM.the_lever_that_already_exists_and_is_alr: pinned.policyBlobs.treatment. It is REQUIRED (the assembler refuses without a {repo, commit, path, sha256} tuple per arm), it is hashed, and voidConditions 12 voids a run whose per-arm policy blob hash is absent from any observation record. A treatment policy that says 'always pass model: <id> to repair/scaffold/implement' pins the model BY an artifact that is already pinned -- no new mechanism, no file outside a repository, and `selection` stops deciding. The control arm has no such tool, so nothing is owed on that side.
_whichModelRunsIsDecidedByRAM.not_adopted_here: Writing that instruction into the treatment policy blob changes what the treatment IS, which is a pre-data design decision and the owner's. Recorded rather than taken. What IS taken: scripts/b12-repair-pace.mjs pins its model explicitly and refuses when it does not fit after unloading, so the MEASUREMENT never silently swaps models even while the RUN still could.

_transport: A plain git fetch brings NO base — measured. Tag auto-following only takes tags pointing into fetched history, and these bases are detached.
Then, ON THE MAC, before spending anything:  node scripts/b12-author.mjs verify-corpus b12-corpus/pilot-plan.json --deep
